content: Discussion thread for #General announcements > EAST labs launhing in Bangalore and #Event announcements > Hackathon: LeanLang for Verified Autonomy

About the Hackathon, you mention Agent System such as OpenClaw, how can we reason about Agent Systems without a Toolchain for the language in which they are written (e.g. Typescript)? Will it be part of the Hackathon to write a Agent System in Lean first so that, we can then build proofs upon that?
The idea will be to have a model of the actions the agent system takes in Lean as well as a DSL or Json schema to interface. Things are proved in Lean

@Franz Huschenbeth Thanks for the question, which made me think further. A good analogue of what we had in mind is the way Lean is used in Cedar whose "programs" are proved in Lean but the actual runtime is Rust.
That said, the intention is to keep things open-ended. If somebody finds a different creative way to verify agents, all the better!

Siddhartha Gadgil said:

Franz Huschenbeth Thanks for the question, which made me think further. A good analogue of what we had in mind is the way Lean is used in Cedar whose "programs" are proved in Lean but the actual runtime is Rust.

So building a protocol model of some agent harness and then proving properties of the protocol. I think it would also be interesting to build a minimal agent harness in Lean, but there is probably a bit of ecosystem / infrastructure missing for that. Maybe one can make a harness, which can just execute bash.

Good point @Franz Huschenbeth - ideally part of the system should be actually in Lean, specially IO and spawning processes (to ensure no agent does rm -rf *:smile:) at least in the longer run. Hopefully as Lean gets it http server and client and stronger FFI more can move there.

For the hackathon maybe the reasonable thing to say is actual running Lean code for part of the system gets extra credit.
